key: Therefore the sage is (like) a square which cuts no one (with its angles); (like) a corner which injures no one (with its sharpness). He is straightforward, but allows himself no license; he is bright, but does not dazzle.
s: Closing a chapter where correction turns to distortion, the text pictures the sage through paired contraries; Wang Bi, on chapter 58, reads it as guiding things away from crookedness without cutting them, and lighting what misleads them without hunting out their hidden faults.

evidence.words: 以方導物，舍去其邪，不以方割物…以光鑑其所以迷，不以光照求其隱慝也
evidence.gloss: With squareness he guides things so that they leave off their crookedness, and does not use squareness to cut things. … With light he illumines what leads them astray, and does not use its shining to search out their hidden wrongs.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 58, at [57]). Wang Bi’s base text (方而不割 … 光而不燿) matches Legge’s lines. His comment on 方而不割 is guiding things with squareness so they leave their crookedness without cutting them; on 光而不燿, using light to show what misleads them without searching out hidden faults. The sentence paraphrases exactly these two comments; “lighting” for 鑑 is a fair rendering. Plain sense (the chapter closes after correction turns to distortion, the sage drawn in contraries) is faithful to day.js and repeats no four words of the key. entry-check ok, 43 words.
